App Preview captions vs screenshot overlays vs listing fields

App Store Connect treats App Preview video copy separately from static screenshot overlays and searchable listing fields on the zh-Hans localization row:

  • App Preview video captions / subtitles — timed text lines that play during autoplay preview video on your product page. Buyers hear or read these while the clip shows your workflow — often with sound off on mobile.
  • App Preview title and description — Connect metadata fields tied to each preview clip in your gallery. They appear below or beside the video player on the storefront.
  • Screenshot overlay captions — static lines on gallery images, not timed to video. Different deliverable — see our screenshot captions guide.
  • Title, subtitle, keywords, description — searchable listing fields. Preview captions do not replace them.

This page covers App Preview video caption and subtitle copy only — not static screenshot overlays, title, subtitle, keyword field, description, What's New, or promotional text. For listing fields, see our China storefront listing guide or description guide.

Where App Preview localization lives in App Store Connect

In App Store Connect, open your app → App Store tab → select the Simplified Chinese (zh-Hans) localization → App Previews and Screenshots. Each App Preview clip in your gallery can carry locale-specific metadata:

  • Preview title — one short line naming the workflow shown in the clip (character limit varies — verify in Connect before you save)
  • Preview description — one or two sentences on what the video demonstrates — not a second full app description
  • Caption / subtitle script — timed lines you or your editor burn into the preview or deliver as closed-caption tracks, depending on your export workflow

US and EU indie teams often upload one English App Preview and reuse it on every locale row. Connect may show the same video file globally while caption text stays English-only — or empty on zh-Hans because nobody localized the script. Empty zh-Hans preview rows fall back to English metadata or silence at autoplay.

Why silent autoplay and English captions fail on the China storefront

App Previews autoplay muted on iPhone by default. On the China storefront, that behavior hits harder when your preview was built for an English-speaking audience:

  • Muted autoplay with English on-screen text — buyers see English captions flash by with no audio context; they assume the app is not maintained for China
  • No captions at all — a workflow demo with no zh-Hans narration or on-screen labels forces buyers to guess what each tap does
  • English voiceover burned in — even when captions exist, an English VO track under muted autoplay reads as foreign; zh-Hans on-screen captions carry the story when sound is off
  • US script pacing — English preview lines written for 15-second US clips often overflow Chinese character widths or appear too long for the same frame timing
  • Mismatch with localized screenshots — zh-Hans gallery frames show Chinese UI while the preview video still narrates in English

Better zh-Hans App Preview captions reduce product-page bounce during the autoplay window — they do not replace in-app UI localization, video re-export, or Apple review decisions. This is copy you paste or hand to your editor, not a video production service.

Character limits and timing on App Preview captions

App Preview caption lines are tighter than description fields — they must fit on screen during autoplay and stay readable at phone width:

  • On-screen caption lines — commonly 6–12 Chinese characters per beat, or roughly one clause per major on-screen action. Longer English brochure lines need splitting into two timed beats.
  • Preview title — one clear clause naming the workflow (verify character cap in Connect — commonly similar to subtitle length)
  • Preview description — one or two sentences; avoid duplicating your full app description
  • Timing sync — each caption beat should align to a visible tap, transition, or result in the clip. We deliver scripts with suggested timecodes when you provide clip duration or an existing English timing sheet.

Chinese preview captions often need fewer characters than English equivalents when phrasing is tight — you do not mirror comma-heavy US marketing lines beat-for-beat. Cut filler adjectives; name the on-screen action in plain zh-Hans.

Common mistakes on zh-Hans App Preview captions

  • Reusing the US App Preview with English burned-in captions on the zh-Hans localization row
  • Pasting Google Translate output that overflows the frame or reads as formal template copy during autoplay
  • Writing preview lines that repeat the app name on every beat instead of naming what happens on screen
  • Matching English word count 1:1 — Chinese lines run longer visually and get clipped mid-sentence
  • Localizing Connect title/description but leaving the caption script English-only — buyers still see foreign text during autoplay
  • Assuming muted autoplay means captions do not matter — on-screen text is often the only narrative when sound is off

Machine translation is fine for internal drafts. Finished App Preview caption copy needs idiomatic zh-Hans timed to your clip — while keeping the product voice of your English originals. AppLocale rewrites preview scripts by hand; we do not deliver raw Google Translate or LLM output as finished copy.

What good zh-Hans App Preview captions look like

Each timed beat should state one concrete on-screen outcome — readable in the second it appears:

  • Beat one mirrors your title's promise: “三秒创建待办” not “欢迎使用我们的应用”
  • Middle beats walk the core workflow — one action per caption, synced to visible taps
  • Final beat can mention pricing or privacy — not unverifiable download counts
  • Preview title: one clause naming the clip's workflow
  • Preview description: what changed in this version of the preview — not marketing boilerplate

zh-Hans preview captions can differ idiomatically from en-US scripts when the on-screen workflow is the same — avoid mirroring English VO pacing that does not fit Chinese reading rhythm.
